title: They look strong in public…
paragraphs:
They look strong in public…
—but heaven sees the fracture.
You can hold a staff… and still be lost.
You can preach truth… and secretly resist it.
And that is where it gets dangerous.

Because the most terrifying leader in Scripture…
is not the obvious villain.

It’s the one who still says “Lord”
but no longer listens.
That kneeling man in the dust?
That’s not just a fallen leader.
That’s us… when pride finally breaks.
Because leadership in the Kingdom was never about position.
And some of us… have been standing too long.
There’s a quiet corruption that doesn’t start in public.
A moment where you knew it was wrong…
And then you led the next day like nothing happened.
“If the blind lead the blind, both will fall into a pit.” (Matthew 15:14)
He wasn’t talking about people who lacked knowledge.
He was talking about people who refused correction.
People who stopped seeing… because they stopped surrendering.
And then comes the hireling heart.
You stay… until it costs you.
You lead… until it demands sacrifice.
“The hired hand runs away because he cares nothing for the sheep.” (John 10:13)
But because he didn’t truly care.
Micah exposed this kind of leader without mercy:
“Her leaders judge for a bribe… yet they lean on the Lord and say, ‘Is not the Lord among us?’” (Micah 3:11)
They were confident in God’s presence…
And then the harshness creeps in.
God speaks directly against that spirit:
“You have ruled them harshly and brutally.” (Ezekiel 34:4)
“You are like whitewashed tombs… outwardly beautiful, but within full of dead bones.” (Matthew 23:27)
Before you think of someone else…
Because this is not just about leaders out there.
This is about the leader you are becoming.
Here’s the truth we don’t like to admit:

You can preach truth
and still hide sin.

You can lead people
and still resist God.

You can look anointed
and still be unrepentant.
Jesus did not come for perfect leaders.
He came for broken ones who will bow.
But when confronted, he didn’t defend himself.
“Create in me a clean heart, O God.” (Psalm 51:10)
And here is the Gospel clearly:
You are not saved by your leadership.
You are not justified by your performance.
You are not cleansed by your image.
You are saved by Jesus Christ alone.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
But God did not leave you there.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Jesus took the weight of your sin.
And through Him, there is not just forgiveness.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9)
Stop leading others where you are unwilling to go.
Like that man in the dust.
Because the greatest leaders in God’s Kingdom…
What have you normalized that God is still calling sin?
Type “OPEN MY HEART” if you’re choosing repentance over performance today.
